title: Circuit characterization of distance reduction for toric ideals of graphs
statement: Let $G$ be a simple graph, let $A_G$ be its incidence matrix, let $I_G$ be the corresponding toric ideal, and let $M$ be a minimal Markov basis for $I_G$. A Markov basis is **distance-reducing** when it has the distance-reduction property for the fibers of $I_G$. **Circuit characterization conjecture.** $M$ is distance-reducing if and only if $M$ reduces the distance of the circuits of $A_G$. This conjecture asserts that, for toric ideals of graphs, it is enough to check distance reduction on circuits. It is proved in the paper when $I_G$ is a complete intersection toric ideal, while the general case remains open.
source_name: Oliver Clarke, Dimitra Kosta and Alexander Milner, “Distance Reduction in Bouquet Decompositions and Toric Ideals of Graphs”, arXiv:2605.13662 (2026).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2024–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2406.17730](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.17730).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.13662

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2026).
